Metadata.title: LumiLattice
Metadata.description: A collaborative AI scientist for optoelectronic materials discovery.

Home.headline: An AI research partner for finding new materials for AR glasses
Home.lead: Test an idea for a new material in seconds. Every number shows where it comes from.

Goal.hint: Set the targets first. Every host and candidate is scored against them, with the evidence behind each verdict.
Goal.note: A band gap of about 3.1 eV puts the absorption edge near 400 nm, the blue end of the visible range.
Goal.title: 1. Research goal
Goal.hintGuided: AR glasses need both of these. The numbers below are a good start for AR, so you can keep them.
Goal.sentence: You are looking for a material that bends light at least as strongly as n = {n}, and lets through visible light longer than {nm} nm.

Guide.label: Workflow steps

hint.goal: Set the minimum n (near 550 nm) and band gap, or keep the AR waveguide defaults.
hint.host: Search Materials Project or COD for a known structure, or upload a CIF.
hint.candidate: Replace part of one element's sites in {host}, then read the structural checks.
hint.evidence: Compare {id} with known materials in the Evidence views, then accept, revise, or reject it with a reason.

Guide.allDone: All four steps are done. Revise the candidate, ask the agent for alternatives, or publish it to the registry.
Guide.exampleStory: SrTiO3 has a high n (2.43, measured) but a band gap near the blue edge of the visible range. LaAlO3 has a wider gap but a lower n (2.07). If La replaces 25% of Sr and Al replaces 25% of Ti, does n stay at 2.2 or more while the gap widens? In "{landscape}", the orange box is the candidate's range between the two end members. Then open "{score}" and "{spatial}".

hintGuided.goal: Keep the goal below or change it. Then pick a starting crystal.
hintGuided.host: Pick one of the four starting crystals, or search for your own.
hintGuided.candidate: Choose which atoms in {host} to swap, or let Muse Spark suggest a swap.
hintGuided.evidence: Read what {id} means, compare it with known materials, then record your decision.

Guide.exampleStoryGuided: SrTiO3 bends light strongly, but it is close to the limit where it starts to absorb violet light. LaAlO3 has more margin, but it bends light less. If we swap a quarter of the Sr for La and a quarter of the Ti for Al, do we gain margin and still bend light enough? The result is below.

Host.hint: Search Materials Project by formula (SrTiO3, *TiO3), elements (Sr,Ti,O), or ID (mp-5229). Or upload your own CIF.

starter.anatase: The white pigment in paint and sunscreen. It bends light very strongly.
starter.zns: A long-used optical material that is clear to the eye.
starter.linbo3: Used in lasers and telecom optics.

Candidate.hint: Replace a fraction of one element's sites in {host}. Atom positions stay at the host positions (no relaxation).

Candidate.viewerLegend: Larger atoms: substituted sites. Pink atoms with labels: atoms in the selected check.
Candidate.noHost: This candidate was opened without a host. You can revise it, or select a host to make new candidates.
Candidate.exportNote: The CIF lists every site (P1) with a provenance header. The JSON record adds the goal score, the 3D structure analysis, the data sources, and the caveats.
Candidate.hintGuided: Choose an element in {host}, the element to put in its place, and how much of it to replace. The app builds the new crystal and checks it.
Candidate.suggest: Let Muse Spark suggest a swap
Candidate.moreTools: More tools: export, relaxation, publishing, lab results
Candidate.mixTitle: Linear mix (a guide; verdicts use the range):
Candidate.mixValues: n ≈ {n} (± about {nError}), band gap ≈ {gap} eV (± about {gapError} eV), from

Critique.title: Muse Spark critique
Critique.aiTag: AI review: an opinion, not evidence
Critique.hint: Muse Spark reviews this candidate from three views of the structure and the computed evidence. Each point cites the evidence it uses, and numbers that are not in the evidence are flagged.
Critique.runningLong: Muse Spark is reviewing {id}. This takes about 30 to 90 seconds.
Critique.noViews: The 3D view could not be captured, so this critique used the evidence only.
Critique.testThis: Ask the agent to test this
Critique.warnings: Problems the checks found in this critique
Critique.hintGuided: Muse Spark looks at pictures of this crystal and at the numbers, then gives a second opinion. Numbers that are not in the evidence are flagged.

Evidence.dftComputed: Computed with density functional theory (DFT). Not a measurement.
Evidence.heuristic: Estimated range from similar materials. Not a prediction.
Evidence.hint: Data behind the host and the current candidate: where they sit among known materials, how n changes with wavelength, the per-site numbers behind each check, and the goal score.
Evidence.needSubject: Select a host or a candidate to see this.
Evidence.title: 5. Evidence
Evidence.hintGuided: See where your starting crystal and your candidate sit among materials that are already known.
Evidence.readLandscape: Each dot is a known material. Up means it bends light more, and right means it stays clearer. AR glasses need the upper-right area, and few dots reach it. That is why new materials are worth looking for.
Evidence.readScore: This is the same result as the summary above, with the source of each number.

Agent.title: 6. Research agent (Muse Spark)
Agent.hint: Ask about the host or a candidate. The agent sees the selected host and candidate, uses tools for every number, and remembers this conversation.
Agent.placeholder: Example: Suggest a substitution for SrTiO3 that keeps the band gap wide.
Agent.noToolCalls: No tool calls in this answer. Treat any numbers in it as unverified.
Agent.hintGuided: Ask anything, even a basic question. Muse Spark can see what you have picked, and it looks up numbers with its tools.
Agent.placeholderGuided: Ask a question in your own words

ask.hard: Why is a clear material that bends light strongly hard to find?

Agent.noToolCallsGuided: This answer did not use the data tools. Treat any numbers in it as unchecked.

Decision.title: Your decision on {id}
Decision.placeholder: Why? e.g. keep Ti4+ only, avoid toxic elements, try a larger A-site ion
Decision.hint: Accept and Reject are recorded. Modify and Explore are recorded and sent to the agent with your reason.
Decision.modifyHint: The agent revises this candidate from your reason.
Decision.exploreHint: The agent tests up to 2 alternatives from your reason.
Decision.rejectHint: Record that this candidate is not useful, and why.
Decision.placeholderGuided: Why? For example: it does not bend light enough, so try another element.
Decision.hintGuided: Your decision is saved with your reason. Modify and Explore also ask Muse Spark to try again, so say what you want changed.

Optical.computed: DFT gaps and n ({count} entries, JARVIS-DFT)
Optical.computedNote: TBmBJ gaps are usually closer to measured gaps than OptB88vdW. n = sqrt(eps) is a long-wavelength value, not n(550 nm).

Publish.demoNote: Candidates are private by default. In this version, publishing only records your choice and credit; nothing is sent outside LumiLattice.
Publish.consent: I choose to make {id} public, with the credit above.

Relax.title: Relaxation (CHGNet, local install)
Relax.hint: Moves atoms and the cell to lower energy with a machine-learned potential, then runs the same checks. Needs PyTorch, so it runs only in a local install.
Relax.energyNote: ML potential; do not compare with DFT energies

Experiment.title: Measurements
Experiment.hint: Add your own measurement to compare prediction and experiment. LumiLattice records it as given and does not verify it.

Registry.title: 7. Candidate registry
Registry.hint: Every candidate on this server, from the form and from the agent. Select up to {max} to compare.

Spatial.distortionSubtitle: Bond-length distortion index Δ of each substituted site's polyhedron
Spatial.distortionNote: Δ = mean |d − d̄| / d̄ (Baur 1974). The shaded zone (Δ > 0.02) marks clearly distorted polyhedra. The table adds quadratic elongation ⟨λ⟩ and bond-angle variance σ² for octahedra.
Spatial.angleSubtitle: Angles through anions shared by two 6-coordinate cations
Spatial.angleNote: Bending below 180° means the octahedra tilt or buckle. Tilt = (180° − angle)/2, reported only for corner-sharing frameworks such as perovskites.
Spatial.noAngles: No corner-sharing octahedra in this structure.
Spatial.orderingTitle: Where the substituted ions sit: ordering energies
Spatial.orderingSubtitle: {total} arrangements in a {cell} repeat of the candidate cell; {distinct} distinct energies
Spatial.orderingAxis: Ewald energy above the lowest arrangement (meV/atom, point charges)
Spatial.allEqual: Every arrangement has the same Ewald energy (same charges), so this model cannot rank them.
Spatial.sampled: Too many arrangements to list all: a reproducible random sample of 300 is shown.

Level.label: Display level
Level.guidedHint: Plain words and the main steps. Technical tools stay one click away.
Level.expertHint: Every tool and number on the screen.

Intro.problemText: AR glasses carry the picture through a thin, clear layer in the lens. The more strongly that layer bends light, the wider the picture can be. But materials that bend light strongly often absorb blue light, so they look yellow. Few materials do both.
Intro.doText: Pick a known crystal and swap some of its atoms for another element. That gives you a new candidate material. You need no lab and no simulation software.
Intro.getText: In seconds: a score against your goal and against known materials, how new the idea looks, where each number comes from, and what to try next. Muse Spark, the AI, can explain the result and suggest changes.
Intro.limit: A candidate is an idea to test, not a proven material. This tool helps you decide which ideas deserve a simulation or a lab sample.

n.name: Refractive index (n)
n.text: How strongly a material bends light. Window glass is about 1.5 and diamond about 2.4. A higher n lets AR glasses show a wider picture.

band_gap.name: Band gap
band_gap.text: The energy, in electronvolts (eV), that light needs before the material can absorb it. Above about 3.1 eV, all visible light passes and the material looks clear. A smaller gap absorbs blue first, so the material looks yellow or dark.

host.name: Starting crystal (host)
host.text: A known material that you change to make a candidate.

candidate.name: Candidate
candidate.text: A new material idea, made by swapping atoms in a starting crystal. Nobody has made or measured it yet.

swap.name: Atom swap (substitution)
swap.text: Some atoms of one element are replaced by another element, in the same positions in the crystal.

cell.name: Unit cell
cell.text: The small box of atoms that repeats in every direction to build the whole crystal.

experimental.name: Experimental
experimental.text: Measured in a lab. This is the strongest kind of evidence here.

dft.name: DFT-computed
dft.text: Calculated by a computer simulation (density functional theory), not measured. Band gaps from it are usually too low.

heuristic.name: Heuristic
heuristic.text: A rough range estimated from similar materials. It is neither a measurement nor a prediction.

mix.name: Straight-line mix
mix.text: A guess that a blend lies part way between its parent materials, in proportion to how much of each it has. Real blends can bend away from this line, so treat it as a guide.

Viewer.controls: Drag to turn. Scroll to zoom.
Viewer.cloudLabel: Cloud picture of the crystal, turning. Soft clouds show where each atom's electrons sit.
Viewer.noWebgl: This browser cannot draw the cloud view (it needs WebGL2).
Viewer.cloudNote: A model picture, not a computed electron density. Cloud size comes from ionic radii, and each cloud stretches along its bonds, weighted by bond strength. White dots mark swapped atoms.
Viewer.flowNote: The ripples only show the direction; electrons do not move like this.

Plain.nScale: Refractive index scale from glass to diamond. Your goal is at least {goal}.
Plain.gapScale: Visible light from blue to red. A band gap of {goal} eV means light longer than {nm} nm passes.

n.meets: It bends light at least as strongly as your goal asks.
n.uncertain: The estimate spans your goal, so it might or might not bend light enough.
n.fails: It bends light less strongly than your goal asks.
n.unknown: No value is known yet, so we cannot tell.

band_gap.meets: It should let through the light your goal asks for.
band_gap.uncertain: The estimate spans your goal, so it might absorb some blue light (striped part).
band_gap.fails: It absorbs light your goal says should pass (dark part), so it would look tinted.
band_gap.unknown: No value is known yet, so we cannot tell.

elements.meets: It has none of the elements you ruled out.
elements.uncertain: We could not fully check the elements.
elements.fails: It has an element you ruled out.
elements.unknown: We could not check the elements.

structure.meets: The quick checks found no obvious problem with how the atoms fit.
structure.uncertain: The quick checks found a possible problem with how the atoms fit. This does not rule it out.
structure.fails: The quick checks found a serious problem with how the atoms fit.
structure.unknown: There is not enough information to check how the atoms fit.

headline.meets: On target. Worth a closer look.
headline.uncertain: It could work, but it is not settled yet.

Plain.subject: Candidate {id} ({formula})
Plain.hostMark: The ring on the scale marks the starting crystal, {formula}.
Plain.caveat: This is an idea to test, not a proven material. The atoms are still at the positions of the starting crystal, and ranges are rough estimates. A simulation or a lab sample is the real test.
Plain.dftGapNote: This value is computed, and computed band gaps usually come out too low, so the real material may be clearer.
Plain.mixN: about {value}, often off by about {error}. The verdict uses the full range.
Plain.mixGap: about {value} eV, often off by about {error} eV. The verdict uses the full range.

Scorecard.title: Score
Scorecard.disqualified: Contains an element you ruled out: {elements}. It goes to the bottom of the ranking.
Scorecard.notProbability: This score ranks ideas. It is not the chance that the material can be made or will work. A wide range means the evidence is weak.

n.name: Bends light
n.why: A higher refractive index lets AR glasses show a wider picture. Reaching your goal earns 70 points.
n.gain: Elements with large, easily distorted electron clouds usually raise n, for example Ti, Nb, or Ta on the metal site. They often narrow the band gap, so check that too.

band_gap.name: Stays clear
band_gap.why: A wide band gap keeps the material clear, so the picture keeps its colors. Reaching your goal earns 70 points.
band_gap.gain: Elements such as Al, Zr, and La usually widen the band gap. They often lower n, so check that too.

trade_off.name: Beats the trade-off
trade_off.why: Usually, when n goes up, the band gap goes down (the Moss relation). A value above 1 beats this trend, and that is what makes a material stand out.
trade_off.gain: This is the hardest metric to move. Compare starting crystals on the chart below, and look for one that is already above the line.

isotropy.name: Same in all directions
isotropy.why: In a cubic crystal, light behaves the same in all directions. In other crystals, light can split, which can blur the picture. The real disordered crystal can keep the symmetry of its starting crystal, so the range runs from the ordered model to the starting crystal.
isotropy.gain: Start from a cubic crystal, or try a smaller swap. A smaller swap is more likely to keep the starting crystal's symmetry.

fit.name: Atoms fit together
fit.why: The quick checks ask if the charges balance, the sizes match, and no atoms overlap. A failed check makes the material less likely to form.
fit.gain: Use a new atom with a similar size and the same charge as the atom it replaces. Open the structure check details to see which check raised a concern.

supply.name: Easy to source
supply.why: Elements produced in only a few countries can be costly or hard to get. Lower production concentration earns more points.
supply.gain: Replace the element with the highest supply risk with one that is produced more widely.

Scorecard.gainTitle: Where to find the most points: {metric}
Scorecard.beats: On the optical metrics alone, this candidate scores higher than {range} of {size} materials with a measured refractive index.
Scorecard.boardHint: Try another swap and see if it climbs. Ranked by the middle of each score range.

tested.title: How well has this been tested?
tested.oxides: Clear oxides: for {inside}% of {cases} measured solid solutions ({systems} chemical systems), the real band gap is inside the range. These values were checked by hand.
tested.oxidesOther: Many of those are one system, MgO–ZnO. Without it, {inside}% of {cases} are inside, and the ranking is weak (rank correlation {rank}). Do not trust small score differences.
tested.semiconductors: Semiconductors: {inside}% of {cases} are inside the band-gap range.
tested.index: Refractive index: only {cases} measured oxide mixes could be tested, and {inside}% are inside the range. Several are thin films, which can have a lower n than bulk crystals.
tested.fit: Atoms fit together: {kept} of {swaps} real compounds keep their points, and {caught} of {implausible} impossible swaps are caught, on swaps kept apart from the design of this rule.
tested.limits: Not tested: whether a high score predicts a material someone can make and use. Values are matched by formula, so the crystal form can differ.

NoveltyCheck.title: How new is it?
NoveltyCheck.hint: This is separate from the score, because a new material is not automatically a good one.
NoveltyCheck.checking: Checking databases and papers. This can take up to a minute…
NoveltyCheck.incomplete: At least one source could not be reached, so this result can change.

known.name: Already known
known.meaning: This exact composition has already been observed. It is not new, but it is a useful reference to compare with.
known.next: Try a partial swap or a different element to move away from it.

computed.name: Computed only
computed.meaning: A database has calculated this exact composition, but we found no record that anyone has made it.
computed.next: Look for papers on it. If there are none, it could be worth a simulation or a lab sample.

related.name: Related work exists
related.meaning: We found no exact match, but researchers have studied this family of materials. Your idea may already be covered in the papers below.
related.next: Read these papers first. Check if they report the same composition, written another way.

unreported.name: Nothing found
unreported.meaning: We found no match in the sources we checked. That makes it worth a closer look. It does not make it a discovery.
unreported.next: Search patents and papers by hand, then confirm it with a simulation and a lab sample.

check.reference: Exact formula in the reference data

templates.chargeFail: No charge-balanced assignment with common oxidation states for {formula}.
templates.distFail: Some atoms are too close (shortest {d} Å, {pair}).
templates.fitLarge: {site}: ion is too large for this site (expected {a} Å, site gives {b} Å, {pct}).
templates.fitSmall: {site}: ion is too small for this site (expected {a} Å, site gives {b} Å, {pct}).
templates.cnMissing: {ion} has no tabulated radius at CN {cn} (nearest tabulated CN {near}): uncommon coordination.
templates.bvsOver: {site}: BVS {bvs} vs {oxi} (overbonded: site too small; bonds would need to change by {d} Å, {pct}).
templates.bvsUnder: {site}: BVS {bvs} vs {oxi} (underbonded: site too large; bonds would need to change by {d} Å, {pct}).
templates.sitesOk: All checked sites are within the heuristic limits.
templates.cnOk: Each ion is tabulated at its coordination number.
templates.tolNa: Applies only to ABX3 perovskite-like structures.
templates.analogNone: No materials database available for analog search.
templates.noAnion: No anion: the checks need an ionic material (oxide, nitride, fluoride).
templates.noRelax1: No relaxation: atoms stay at the host positions, so the checks show how well the new elements fit the host geometry.
templates.noRelax2: A real material would adjust its lattice.
templates.relaxed1: Relaxed with CHGNet (machine-learned potential): atoms and cell moved to lower energy, so the checks describe the relaxed geometry.
templates.mDistance: Overlap below {a} Å or cation-anion below {b} x radius sum
templates.mCn: First anion shell within {x} x shortest distance; Shannon (1976) ionic radii
templates.mBvs: Bond valence sum, O'Keeffe & Brese (1991) universal parameters, b = {b} Å; implied bond change warn >{w}, fail >{f}
templates.mTol: t = (r_A + r_X) / (sqrt(2) (r_B + r_X)); Shannon (1976) ionic radii, A at CN 12, B at CN 6
templates.mAnalog: Materials Project formula search (end members of each substitution)
templates.goalDftGap: DFT gaps can differ from measured gaps by up to about 1 eV.
templates.bulkMedian: 550 nm, bulk; median of {k} sources ({a}–{b}, e.g. o/e directions).
templates.match: Matched by formula; the polymorph may differ from the selected structure.
templates.dftN: n = sqrt(eps) from DFT linear optics (electronic, zero frequency): long-wavelength limit, not n(550 nm).
templates.gapNote: Reported in the literature; the compilation does not record the measurement method.
templates.minedMedian: Median of {k} values text-mined from papers (middle half {a}–{b} eV).
templates.minedNote: Text mining makes errors, and the papers can report films, nanoparticles, or doped samples.
templates.gapMbj: TBmBJ gaps are usually close to measured gaps.
templates.gapOpt: OptB88vdW (GGA-type) gaps are usually too small.
templates.rangeNot: Not a prediction: it assumes the value lies between them, and it can mix measured and DFT values.
templates.rangeWideN: Widened by {m} on each side, from tests on computed mixes.
templates.rangeWideGap: Widened by {m} eV on each side, from tests on measured oxide solid solutions.
templates.rangeFew: Not enough end-member data ({names}) for a range.
templates.landMeasured: Measured: refractiveindex.info bulk n at 550 nm, with a measured band gap (Zhuo et al. 2018 or Dong & Cole 2022) or, as an open ring, the JARVIS TBmBJ band gap.
templates.landComputed: Computed: JARVIS TBmBJ gap and n = sqrt(eps), a long-wavelength value (an evenly spaced sample of {k} entries).
templates.landMoss: Moss relation (n^4 * Eg = 95 eV) is an empirical trend, not a limit.
templates.mixNote1: End-member values weighted by each one's share of the composition.
templates.mixNote2: A guide, not a prediction: real mixes can bend away from a straight line.
templates.mixNote3: Verdicts and the score use the range.
templates.mpN: n = sqrt(eps_electronic): long-wavelength limit, not n(550 nm)
templates.mpGap: DFT band gaps are usually lower than measured gaps
templates.mpHull: thermodynamic stability at 0 K; not a synthesis prediction
templates.siteSpread: farthest-point: replaced sites are spread as far apart as possible (deterministic; one of many possible orderings, not energy-ranked)
templates.siteOne: every site is replaced, so there is one arrangement
templates.siteLowest: lowest Ewald energy: the lowest of all {k} arrangements of these dopants in a {cell} cell (formal charges, unscreened point charges: relaxation can change the order)
templates.siteSeeded: lowest Ewald energy found by a seeded search (random sample, then greedy swaps) over {k} arrangements in a {cell} cell; not guaranteed to be the lowest (formal charges, unscreened point charges: relaxation can change the order)
templates.errFractions: Fractions for {el} add up to {total}, more than 1.
templates.errSupercell1: These fractions need a supercell that is too large.
templates.errSupercell2: Use fractions such as 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6, or 1/8 of the sites.
templates.errEwald: The lowest-Ewald arrangement needs formal charges, so the material must have an anion.
templates.spMethod: Ewald summation with formal (average) charges in a repeated cell; a point-charge model for ranking only
templates.spNote2: An ordered supercell is one model of a disordered solid solution; its symmetry and arrangement are properties of that model.
templates.spNote3: Small supercells cannot show every tilt pattern (many need a √2 × √2 or larger cell).
templates.spNoAnion: No anion: polyhedral analysis needs an ionic material.
templates.spBire: In this ordered model the material would be birefringent if the class is not isotropic.
templates.spChains: {el} ions repeat every {d} Å along the shortest cell axis (their own periodic images): the cell is one host cell thick there, so every arrangement in it has these chains.
templates.spThicker: A thicker cell would separate them.
templates.spClustered: {el} ions sit on neighboring sites ({d} Å): clustered.
templates.spSameEnergy: Every arrangement has the same Ewald energy (same charges), so the point-charge model cannot rank them; size effects need relaxation (CHGNet).
templates.spRank: This ordering ranks {r} of {k} distinct arrangements by Ewald energy (+{e} meV/atom above the lowest).
templates.spRankSample: This ordering ranks {r} of {k} distinct arrangements (random sample) by Ewald energy (+{e} meV/atom above the lowest).
templates.relaxMethod: CHGNet {v} pretrained ML potential (package {p}), cell and positions relaxed, fmax {f} eV/Å, at most {s} steps
templates.relaxLocal: CHGNet relaxation is available only in a local install (cd backend && uv sync --group relax).
templates.scGap: Band gap {v} eV against a goal of {g} eV ({s}).
templates.scUnknown: {label} is unknown, so this metric counts as 0 to 100.
templates.scMossUnknown: n or the band gap is unknown, so this metric counts as 0 to 100.
templates.scIso: An isotropic crystal has one n in all directions, so light does not split.
templates.scSym: The symmetry could not be determined.
templates.scNoSupply: No supply data for at least one element.
templates.method1: Weights: n and band gap 60 together, n-gap trade-off 10, optical isotropy 10, atom fit 15, element supply 5. n and the band gap are combined as a geometric mean, because AR glasses need both and one cannot make up for the other.
templates.method2: The goal value earns 70 points on each.
templates.method3: A range is the worst and best end of the evidence, and a metric with no data counts as 0 to 100.
templates.method4: This score ranks ideas; it is not a probability that the material can be made or will work.
templates.bench1: Materials with a measured n at 550 nm in refractiveindex.info, scored on the three optical metrics.
templates.bench2: This set favors materials already used in optics, not all of them have a measured band gap, and some reports are doubtful (BP is listed at 4.2 eV).
templates.nov1: This checks Materials Project, COD, the bundled reference data, and paper titles from OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, and Semantic Scholar.
templates.nov2: It cannot check patents, unpublished work, or papers that write the composition another way.
templates.nov3: Not found does not mean new.
